description: Conformance transcript for the client-driven relay (the `game` lane, PROTOCOL.md section 3.10). This is the ORACLE a second implementation (e.g. a native daemon) A/Bs its wire output against: for each `in` frame, on a connection in the named state, the server emits exactly the frames in `out` (to the named connections) and nothing to the connections in `silent`. Connection A is subscribed to the topic and granted publish; B is subscribed to the topic (a receiver); D is neither subscribed nor granted. `seq` is the per-topic session-home counter (starts at 1, stamped only on a relayed frame - a denial consumes none). Validated live against the reference server in test/relay-oracle.test.js.

transcript.step: granted, id present -> fan out to the room excluding the sender, seq 1, id echoed
granted, no id -> seq increments to 2, envelope carries no id
granted but non-string event -> game-denied INVALID to the sender only, id echoed, no fan out, no seq consumed
never granted -> game-denied FORBIDDEN to the sender only
after revoke, a formerly-granted connection is FORBIDDEN again, id echoed

binaryTwin.description: The 0x03 binary twin (ingress kind `game:1`, PROTOCOL.md section 6.6) of the FIRST transcript step: the same event/data/id carried compact-encoded instead of as a JSON `game` frame, producing the identical fan-out. Layout [0x03][schemaVersion:u8][ingressId:varint][seq:varint][payload], payload = encodeValue(['move',{dx:1,dy:0},5]) (the generic value codec, PROTOCOL.md 6.3). The frame's own seq is the per-binding ingress counter; the ROOM seq is stamped on fan-out (1). A native decoder A/Bs against this.
